title: the return
hook: a victorious army of monkeys raids the king's private honey orchard, and the king hears the complaint and starts to smile

segments.voice: Yesterday: the return. Arishta sinking, the sky like an ocean, and your line, the roar, and the knowing, before the words came.

On the way home to Kishkindha, the triumphant search party comes to the Madhuvana, the honey forest: King Sugriva's private, carefully guarded orchard. And they are very, very hungry. Big wins can come with a celebration that gets a little out of hand, and the Sundara Kanda has one too. It's wonderfully undignified.
screen: `THE MADHUVANA, THE HONEY FOREST.` → `A CELEBRATION OUT OF HAND.`

segments.voice: First, a serious moment. After Hanuman's report, Angada has a bold idea: why not go back to Lanka ourselves, defeat Ravana, and bring Sita to Rama? Jambavan, the old bear, says no. Our task was to find her and to tell Rama. The rescue is Rama's to make, as Sita herself said in the grove: let Rama come. So they set off north. Then the Madhuvana. With Angada's permission, the monkeys fall on the honey. They eat it, drink it, dance, sing, wrestle, tumble out of the trees, stagger about, and Valmiki tells it with obvious enjoyment. The orchard's guardian is Dadhimukha, Sugriva's uncle, and when he tries to stop them, they shove him around. Furious, he rushes to King Sugriva. Your honey forest is ruined; Angada's band has torn it to pieces. And Sugriva's reaction is the best part. He's not angry. He's thrilled. He turns to Rama and Lakshmana and says, in effect: they would never dare do this unless they'd succeeded. They've found Sita. A wrecked orchard becomes good news for Rama, at last. Sugriva reads the mess the way Jambavan read the roar on the shore. Dadhimukha is sent back to tell the monkeys to come at once. And Hanuman is about to stand in front of Rama.
screen: `LET RAMA MAKE THE RESCUE.` · `THE MONKEYS RAID THE HONEY.` · `DADHIMUKHA COMPLAINS TO SUGRIVA.` · then, large: `THEY'D NEVER DARE UNLESS...`

segments.voice: Picture a recent mess in your life, a cluttered kitchen after a meal, toys on the floor, a noisy room, and instead of seeing only the mess, ask what it says: people ate together, children played, something happened. Breathe in and let the mess tell its story; breathe out and let a little of the irritation go.
The return. Jambavan leaves the rescue to Rama, the monkeys raid Sugriva's honey forest, and Sugriva reads the wreckage as proof that Sita has been found.
Your line: a wrecked orchard, good news. Tomorrow, Hanuman stands in front of Rama at last. See you there.

howItsDone: The Madhuvana episode is a comic interlude in Sundara Kanda recitations and children's retellings, and storytellers enjoy Sugriva's delighted reading of the complaint.

original.note: Sanskrit madhuvana: madhu, honey, and vana, forest or grove.

chat.says: Why was King Sugriva happy when he heard the monkeys had wrecked his orchard?
options: They'd never dare do that unless they'd succeeded, so he knew Sita was found.
He'd always disliked that orchard and was glad to see it gone.
He thought the monkeys had earned a treat after a long, failed search.
chat.meaning: Sugriva read the mess correctly: the monkeys would never dare raid his honey forest unless they'd found Sita.
